question: Is the initial experimental `claws update` contract allowed to ship with fail-closed `update_partial` and manual status/Doctor inspection, or must it include durable operation-identity reconciliation before any mutating executor lands?
rationale: The code can report uncertain external mutation, but the acceptable operator recovery guarantee is a product and lifecycle-policy choice rather than a mechanical patch decision.

options.title: Require boundary proof and explicit recovery acceptance
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed design, but require exact-head package and Gateway failure/retry proof plus maintainer approval of the documented status/Doctor recovery flow before merge.

options.title: Sponsor the partial-state contract as-is
options.body: Accept `update_partial` with manual operator recovery as the experimental contract, documenting the operational support expectation in the PR discussion.

options.title: Defer mutation until reconciliation is durable
options.body: Pause this executor until it can persist an operation identity and reconcile uncertain external mutations without relying on manual investigation.

recommendation.title: Require boundary proof and explicit recovery acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep the current fail-closed design, but require exact-head package and Gateway failure/retry proof plus maintainer approval of the documented status/Doctor recovery flow before merge.
